problem_statement: PSA Crypto must be able to serialize a key slot to a compact CBOR byte representation and parse it back. Provide psa_encode_key_slot() to encode a psa_key_slot_t into a caller-supplied buffer and report the encoded length through an output parameter; psa_decode_key_attributes() to read the attributes from such a buffer into a psa_key_attributes_t; and psa_decode_key_slot_data() to read the key material from the same buffer into the slot. The encoded form is a two-element array: first an attributes array holding id, type, bits, lifetime, and a usage/algorithm pair; second the key material. A single key encodes its key bytes as a bytestring; an asymmetric key pair encodes an array of the private key and public key bytestrings; a protected key encodes an array of slot number, optionally followed by a public key bytestring for an asymmetric protected slot. The psa_key_pair_slot_t and psa_prot_key_slot_t types used by the tests must be available. Decoding a valid encoding must restore both the attributes and the key data, with psa_decode_key_attributes() called before psa_decode_key_slot_data().

verification.reason: The only missing piece is the public header name psa_crypto_cbor_encoder.h that the tests include; the statement describes the functions and their behaviour but never tells the agent which header to place them in. This is a straightforward missing-name problem that can be repaired by adding the header path to the statement.

problems.detail: The tests include the header "psa_crypto_cbor_encoder.h" to obtain the declarations of psa_encode_key_slot(), psa_decode_key_attributes(), and psa_decode_key_slot_data(), but the problem statement never names this header. Without knowing the exact filename the agent must create, the test will fail to compile.

verification.note: second review: 'the CBOR encoding must be used to implement persistent storage' reworded as a requirement

problem_statement_fixed:
PSA Crypto must be able to serialize a key slot to a compact CBOR byte representation and parse it back. Provide psa_encode_key_slot() to encode a psa_key_slot_t into a caller-supplied buffer and report the encoded length through an output parameter; psa_decode_key_attributes() to read the attributes from such a buffer into a psa_key_attributes_t; and psa_decode_key_slot_data() to read the key material from the same buffer into the slot. These three functions must be declared in a header file named psa_crypto_cbor_encoder.h. The encoded form is a two-element array: first an attributes array holding id, type, bits, lifetime, and a usage/algorithm pair; second the key material. A single key encodes its key bytes as a bytestring; an asymmetric key pair encodes an array of the private key and public key bytestrings; a protected key encodes an array of slot number, optionally followed by a public key bytestring for an asymmetric protected slot. The psa_key_pair_slot_t and psa_prot_key_slot_t types used by the tests must be available. Decoding a valid encoding must restore both the attributes and the key data, with psa_decode_key_attributes() called before psa_decode_key_slot_data().

Persistent key storage must also be provided, as the build module psa_persistent_storage. When a key with a persistent lifetime is imported or generated, it must be stored persistently. When a key is looked up by ID and is not found in volatile memory, it must be loaded from persistent storage. Attempting to import or generate a key whose ID already exists in persistent storage must return PSA_ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS. Destroying a persistent key must remove it from persistent storage, and subsequent operations on that key ID must return PSA_ERROR_DOES_NOT_EXIST. A persistent key must remain accessible even after its volatile key slot is reused for another key.
